structs.name: DiskReadContext

Game-test 64 has an extra 8-byte m_lastStartReadTime at +32 that no Replay code touches.

DiskFS::StartRead@0x140f63110: `*(_QWORD *)(i+40) = callbackArg`, passed back as the callback's first argument

structs.notes: Two Replay pool owners are involved: the entries live in DiskFS (see DiskFS below). The packet's replay_functions entry DiskFile::StartRead@0x140f62d20 takes a DiskFile this, not a read context, so its +256..+296 accesses do not describe this struct; DiskFS::StartRead is the real user. Applying the 56-byte size requires the DiskFS pool (m_reads) to change to DiskReadContext[256] = 14336 bytes at DiskFS+79880.

structs.name: DiskFS
structs.size_evidence: tail closure (method 4 + 6): the last member m_reads is the DiskReadContext pool at Replay +79880 (DiskFS::StartRead@0x140f63110: `i = this + 79880`, stride 56, 256 entries) = 14336 bytes, so the end is 79880 + 14336 = 94216; DiskFS alignment is 8 (vtable at +0) and 94216 % 8 = 0. Global extent check (method 5): DB_DiskFSInitialize@0x140f633d0 returns the global s_dbDiskFSState@0x1441B6230; the next named global is at 0x1441CD248, a gap of 94232 bytes, so 94216 <= size <= 94232, consistent. The builder size 94216 agrees.
members: DiskFS_vftable is the vtable name at +0 (the base class DB_FileSysInterface's pointer). The stores are not seen in the decompiled methods (DB_DiskFSInitialize only returns the global), so the vtable itself is UNCONFIRMED; the 8-byte slot is real because DiskFS methods are reached through it

DiskFS_OpenFileHandle@0x140f62c40: `v9 = diskFs + 8`, `v9 += 312`, 256 entries ('DiskFS: Out of file handles (%d)'), handle at +264, flags at +304, path copied to +0; DiskFS::Shutdown@0x140f62bc0: `v2 = a1 + 8`, `v2 += 312`, 256 iterations, `*(QWORD*)(v2+264) != -1` leak test. So m_files is 256 * 312 = 79872 bytes (game-test DiskFile is 288, so the game-test 73728 does not apply)
DiskFS::StartRead@0x140f63110: pool base this+79880, stride 56, 256 entries, Sys_Error 'Out of read contexts (256)'; entry layout as DiskReadContext
unconfirmed: baseclass_0 (vtable slot at +0): the DiskFS_vftable store was not decompiled
structs.notes: DiskFile is 312 bytes in Replay, not the 288 game-test and the A115 range assume. Proven fields of one DiskFile entry: path char[256] at +0 (copied by DiskFS_OpenFileHandle), state int at +256 (set to 1 on open), handle HANDLE at +264 (ReadFileEx / SetFilePointerEx / Shutdown leak test), fileFlags DWORD at +304 (`& 8` = async, checked in DiskFS::StartRead and DiskFS_ReadBlocking). The IDA DiskFile layout (lastReadEndOffset +256, lastStartReadTime +264, handle +272) disagrees with all of this; flag it to the DiskFile owner (A115 range) with size 312. DiskFS::Seek@0x140f62f50, DiskFS::Exists, DiskFS_ReadBlocking@0x140f63020 and DiskFS_WaitForFile take diskFile/reservedCtx, not DiskFS fields past +8, so nothing in them reaches past 94216.

structs.name: InviteJoinHSM_xb3
structs.size_evidence: method 2 (deleting destructor): InviteJoinHSM_xb3::scalar_deleting_dtor@0x141b30470 stores `InviteJoinHSM_xb3_vftable` at [rcx] (so it sits in xb3's own vtable), calls ~InviteJoinHSM_xb3@0x140f1bd30, then `mov edx, 320h` (800) and `bdMemory::deallocate_5` when deleteFlags bit 0 is set. Sized free of 800 = sizeof(InviteJoinHSM_xb3). The base's own deleting dtor InviteJoinHSM::scalar_deleting_dtor@0x140f1bd90 also frees 800 (`mov edx, 320h`) after storing InviteJoinHSM_vftable, so the base is 800 too and xb3 adds no own bytes.

structs.notes: xb3 has no own members in Replay; every xb3 method reads base offsets (+8, +192, +340, +348, +392, +656, +660, +784 per the packet). The IDA _pad320 is wrong. For the A100 owner: InviteJoinHSM is 800 bytes by the base's own deleting dtor, and the base ctor in Replay writes +656 as qword -1, +664 as dword -1, +668 byte, +669 word, +672 dword, +676 byte, +680 dword, +696 dword, +712 dword, +720 dword, +728..+752 qwords, +760 dword, +768/+776 qwords, +784 byte, +788 qword, so the first pass's '+656/+660 int pair' reading is not the whole story. The name 'InviteJoinHSM_xb3::~InviteJoinHSM_xb3' at 0x140f1bd30 is correctly named (it is the body called from the scalar dtor). No renames.
